summary.en-US: Hierarchical outline and timeline scrubber for Project Gutenberg books — jump chapters fast, scrub the whole text, and read in built-in dark mode.

description.en-US:
Project Gutenberg Outline turns long Gutenberg HTML books into something you can actually navigate.

When you open a book on gutenberg.org, the extension builds a structured outline and a right-edge timeline so you can move by chapter, subsection, or scroll position — without endless page scrolling.

Features

  • Hierarchical outline — parts, chapters, and numbered subsections, auto-detected from the book markup and text patterns.
  • Timeline scrubber — a slim rail of ticks on the right edge; hover for a preview, wheel to step one-by-one, click to jump.
  • Split peek — Shift+click an outline row or tick to read a passage in place without losing your spot.
  • Return to reading spot — jumping via the outline stacks your previous scroll position (Alt+←).
  • Built-in book dark mode — darkens the Gutenberg page for night reading; toggle with ☾ in the drawer or press D. Preference is saved. The outline UI stays consistent either way.
  • Search — filter the outline by chapter title or quote text.

Shortcuts

  • Ctrl/Cmd + \ — open or close the outline drawer
  • D — toggle book dark mode
  • Alt + ← — return to previous reading spot

Privacy

  • Runs only on Project Gutenberg book HTML pages.
  • Permission: storage (dark-mode preference only).
  • No accounts, no analytics, no remote code, no network calls.

Notes

Designed for *.gutenberg.org cached EPUB HTML and /files/ book pages. Outline quality depends on each book’s heading structure; the extension also synthesizes subsections from numbered paragraphs and long unheaded stretches.

release_notes.en-US: Initial AMO release: hierarchical outline, timeline scrubber, split peek, return-to-spot, and built-in book dark mode for Project Gutenberg HTML texts.
